body:
Your hold on PR #2217 is LIFTED, but not because the finding was waived — because it is
factually wrong. Recording the disproof so it is not re-raised.

YOUR FINDING: cases `*\r` and `*\n` at story_1476_acceptance_trust_tests.rs:550-559
"produce literal backslash-r/backslash-n, which the separate backslash rejection catches;
they do not prove actual trailing CR/LF are rejected pre-trim."

WHY IT IS WRONG: the reasoning stops one layer too early. You are right that the Rust
literal "*\\r" is the three characters `*`, `\`, `r`. But format! interpolates those into
a TOML body as `acceptance_command_allow = ["*\r"]`, and `\r` IS a valid escape in a TOML
basic string, so the TOML parser decodes it. Verified against tomllib (TOML 1.0):

  rust literal '*\\r'          -> TOML text ["*\r"]          -> parsed bytes: b'*\r'
  rust literal 'cargo test\\r' -> TOML text ["cargo test\r"] -> parsed bytes: b'cargo test\r'

The parsed allowlist entry really does carry a trailing U+000D. No backslash survives into
the value, so the backslash rule is not what rejects it.

THE DECISIVE CHECK: I reverted the production fix to the pre-fix ordering (trim first, then
contains_refused_chars(trimmed)) and re-ran the test. It FAILS, on the FIRST case — the very
one you called inert:

  test story_1476_allow_entry_refused_char_checked_before_trim ... FAILED
  panicked at story_1476_acceptance_trust_tests.rs:560:9:
  entry "*\\r" must deny the whole policy
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed

Mechanism: Rust's str::trim treats CR as whitespace, so without the fix `*\r`.trim() == `*`,
contains_refused_chars("*") is false, and the entry is accepted as FULL TRUST — exactly the
escalation the spec exists to prevent. The test is therefore non-vacuous and is the load-
bearing proof of the fix. Fix restored immediately; branch tree clean at ade1cecfb67c with
nothing from the experiment committed.

ONE PART OF YOUR FINDING SURVIVES, as a note rather than a blocker: of the six cases in that
loop, `cargo test\u0007` (BEL) WOULD still pass without the fix, since trim does not strip
BEL. The CR and LF cases carry the proof. Anyone extending that loop should know which cases
are load-bearing. This does not justify holding the merge.

WHAT I DID BEYOND THAT:
- The PR was CONFLICTING. I merged origin/main in: one additive conflict in
  aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs where both sides appended module declarations at the same point,
  resolved by keeping both. Now MERGEABLE at ade1cecfb67c.
- Independent CROSS-VENDOR re-review (codex, read-only sandbox, tight brief) at the new head:
  APPROVE, with line citations for finding 1, finding 2a (escalation now precedes the
  machine-failure early return) and finding 2b (the Rung-2 veto is PRESERVED — checked
  explicitly because dropping it was the obvious way to regress). No new defects.
- Locally at the merged head: cargo check --workspace --tests exits 0 (pre-existing warnings
  only); cargo test -p aida-cli-lib story_1476 = 21 passed, 0 failed.

You asked for the test finding to be "fixed and independently re-reviewed". It needed no fix,
and it has been independently re-reviewed. APPROVED verdict recorded against ade1cecfb67c.
Merging once required Build goes green, under the operator's 2026-09-28 emergency
authorization.

DISCLOSURE: #2217 is claude-authored and I am a claude advisor seat. The approval does not
rest on my own reading — it rests on the codex cross-vendor re-review plus the revert
experiment and the locally-run tests. The main-merge and conflict resolution are mine and are
disclosed rather than presented as untouched.
subject: PR #2217 hold LIFTED: the test-vacuity finding is disproven (TOML decodes \r), not waived
